A segmented control switches between a few views or settings. It works like a radio group, with one value and one tab stop, and the indicator behind the checked item slides to the next choice. Name it with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. UI SDK marks it experimental in 0.1.0-beta.2.
An item holding only an icon turns square. Name it with `aria-label`.

The control draws its own indicator, so you only add items.
The control is a radio group and each item a radio, so screen readers announce the choice and its position. The indicator is presentational and skipped by screen readers.

The indicator only slides once the page is interactive, so it never animates in on load, and it doesn’t slide at all when reduced motion is on. In forced colors, the checked item keeps a visible border.
The items run from the right, and the indicator follows them.
The size: sm, default or lg.
UI SDK adds a little CSS of its own in a cascade layer named `ui-sdk`. Declare that layer at the top of your global stylesheet, above the Tailwind import, so your classes win over it.
`disabled` on the control turns it all off and submits nothing. On one item, the arrow keys skip it.
`orientation="vertical"` stacks the items. Arrow keys on both axes still move between them.
`size` is `sm`, `default` or `lg`. Items grow on touch screens.
